# disrobe

> One tool to decompile, deobfuscate, and unpack compiled software, deterministically, in a single Rust binary. disrobe is a multi-language decompiler, deobfuscator, and unpacker covering Python, JavaScript, WebAssembly, .NET, JVM, Android, Go, Lua, PHP, Ruby, native PE/ELF/Mach-O, and more, behind one CLI with a deterministic pass pipeline that records exactly what it recovered and what it could not.

Strong recovery claims are measured against independent references. Coverage self-reports are labeled, scoped to their inspected populations, and never presented as external correctness. The hosted docs live at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/ and a browser playground at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/playground/.

disrobe is proprietary, source-available software under the Disrobe Source-Available License, Version 1.1: free only for individuals' own hobby, learning, and independent security research, nonprofit education and research, and bona fide journalism, always with credit to 1-3-7; any company or for-profit use requires a paid license; redistribution, forks, rebranding, hosted offerings, and competing development are prohibited; the software is provided as is. The name "disrobe" is reserved. A full single-file copy of these docs for ingestion lives at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/llms-full.txt.

## Introduction

- [Introduction](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/introduction.html): Recover source, unpack payloads, and trace the evidence back to the input.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/installation.html): Install disrobe from GitHub Releases or build the CLI from source.
- [Quickstart](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/quickstart.html): This walkthrough takes a local file through automatic recovery, inspects the result, and shows how to select a direct command when you know the format.
- [Reading a result](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/reading-a-result.html): Start by confirming the input identity, then inspect the recovered artifacts and the stages that stopped.

## Architecture

- [Overview](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/architecture.html): disrobe is a workspace of focused Rust crates exposed through one CLI.
- [The five-rung IR ladder](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/ir-ladder.html): Disrobe uses five intermediate representations, from original bytes to rendered source.
- [Passes and pass selection](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/passes.html): A pass is the unit of work in disrobe.
- [The chain runner](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/chain.html): The chain runner detects each artifact, runs a matching recovery pass, and routes its output to the next pass.
- [The .dr envelope](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/envelope.html): The .dr envelope is disrobe's content-addressed IR wire format.
- [Metadata sidecar and provenance](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/llm-sidecar.html): disrobe can emit a structured metadata bundle beside recovered output.

## Reverse-engineering toolkit

- [Supported families catalog](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/catalog.html): This is the authoritative per-ecosystem list of every packer, obfuscator, protector, freezer, and bundler disrobe recognizes, with the support tier for each.
- [Anti-analysis defeat](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/anti-analysis.html): disrobe analyzes samples statically by default.
- [Queryable IR and capabilities](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/query.html): disrobe query and disrobe capabilities turn a stripped binary into something you can interrogate.
- [Recon, prowl, and indicators](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/frisk.html): disrobe frisk scans files, directories, APKs, and recovered source trees for secrets and indicators.

## Language and format guides

- [Python](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/python.html): disrobe disassembles and decompiles Python bytecode across CPython 1.0-3.15 and the alternative runtimes, peels source-level obfuscators, and unwraps freezers and protectors back to .pyc.
- [JavaScript / TypeScript](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/javascript.html): disrobe reverses supported JavaScript and TypeScript obfuscation, extracts modules from recognized bundle layouts, and inspects packaged JavaScript runtimes.
- [Webview desktop frontends](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/webview.html): disrobe webview statically recovers the frontend files embedded in Electron, Tauri, and Wails desktop applications.
- [WebAssembly](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/wasm.html): disrobe parses WebAssembly modules, lifts them to four target surfaces, reverses Wasm-specific obfuscators, and decodes the Component Model and GC type graphs.
- [JVM and Android](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/jvm-android.html): disrobe decompiles JVM classfiles and Android DEX through a unified command, adding protector analysis, ProGuard/R8 mapping reports, and chain auto-detection, with headless wrappers for FOSS decompilers selected by the format's default routing or --backend.
- [.NET / CIL](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/dotnet.html): disrobe parses .NET PE and CLR metadata, decompiles CIL to C#, F#, and VB pseudo-source, registers detection and routing for <!-- m:dotnet_protectors -->23<!-- /m --> protector families, and probes ReadyToRun and Native AOT images.
- [Native (PE / ELF / Mach-O / NE)](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/native.html): disrobe includes native decompilation for x86-64, AArch64, ARM32, and MIPS32, alongside symbol recovery, disassembly, identification, patching, fingerprinting, and diffing.
- [Native decompile](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/native-decompile.html): disrobe's x86-64 decompiler emits C or Rust.
- [Native unpacking and devirtualization](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/native-unpack.html): disrobe detects the runtime packer on a PE / ELF / Mach-O and unpacks it, driving stub-based packers through an in-house x86 emulator, and lifts bytecode-VM protected code back to IR and pseudo-code.
- [Go](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/go.html): disrobe recovers symbols from stripped and garbled Go binaries across PE, ELF, and Mach-O by parsing the Go runtime's own metadata tables.
- [Lua](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/lua.html): disrobe decompiles compiled Lua chunks across every common dialect, peels the major Lua obfuscators, and devirtualizes custom-VM wrappers back to runnable Lua source.
- [PHP](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/php.html): disrobe peels PHP eval chains, evaluates supported decode loops and literal-key ciphers, and extracts Phar members.
- [Ruby](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/ruby.html): disrobe analyzes Ruby artifacts and recovers source from YARV and mruby bytecode.
- [BEAM (Erlang / Elixir)](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/beam.html): disrobe parses BEAM IFF files, recovers Erlang or Elixir source when debug chunks survive, lifts to Core Erlang otherwise, and disassembles the Code chunk per instruction.
- [Swift / Objective-C](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/swift.html): disrobe extracts the type metadata the Objective-C and Swift runtimes leave in a native binary, demangles it, parses SwiftShield rename mappings into a lookup for downstream use, and rebuilds the dylibs a dyld shared cache bundles into standalone Mach-O images.
- [ActionScript 3 / Flash](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/as3.html): disrobe parses SWF files, disassembles their embedded ActionScript 3 bytecode (AVM2), and lifts method bodies back to readable AS3 pseudocode via operand-stack abstract interpretation.
- [Mobile (Hermes / Flutter)](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/mobile.html): disrobe detects the runtime inside a mobile package, extracts React Native and other bundles, lifts Hermes bytecode to a JavaScript surface, and recovers Dart source or disassembles the ARM64 AOT snapshot from Flutter artifacts.
- [Python pickle](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/pickle.html): disrobe analyzes pickles statically so you can audit what a stream would do on load before it ever touches a real interpreter.
- [Shell / PowerShell](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/shell.html): disrobe deobfuscates supported PowerShell, Bash, Batch, VBScript, and VBA patterns.
- [Containers and archives](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/containers.html): Before disrobe can decompile anything, it often has to get inside a container.

## Reference

- [Global flags](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/global-flags.html): These flags are accepted on every subcommand (they are declared global = true on the root parser).
- [Command reference](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/reference.html): disrobe <command> --help is authoritative for the binary you are running; the surface changes with optional build features.
- [Project configuration](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/config.html): disrobe reads an optional .disrobe.toml so a project can set its own defaults instead of repeating the same global flags on every invocation.
- [Batch directory processing](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/batch.html): disrobe auto accepts a directory as well as a single file.
- [Run reports](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/report.html): ﻿# Run reports (disrobe report)
- [Analysis-depth commands](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/analysis-depth.html): A set of static-analysis primitives that make disrobe useful as a triage and reverse-engineering tool, not only a decompiler.
- [Diff and guard tooling](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/diff-guard.html): disrobe treats recovered artifacts as a forensic baseline you can diff across versions and protect against tampering.
- [The daemon: HTTP, gRPC, LSP, MCP](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/serve.html): disrobe serve exposes byte classification and envelope operations over HTTP and gRPC, classification and error lookup over LSP, and pass-specific analysis, recovery, and workspace tools over MCP.
- [Signed WebAssembly plugins](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/plugin.html): disrobe plugin runs a third-party analysis component through the disrobe-plugin-host sandbox.
- [Use it as a library](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/library.html): Use Disrobe through its Rust crates, Python bindings, or service protocols.
- [Python bindings](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/python-bindings.html): Use Disrobe's recovery engines from Python to decompile bytecode, analyze native code, deobfuscate scripts, and extract packaged files.
- [The browser playground](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/playground.html): The playground analyzes files in your browser using the WebAssembly build of Disrobe.
- [Forensics and malware-safety posture](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/forensics-safety.html): Analysts run disrobe against hostile input that must not detonate.
- [Threat model](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/threat-model.html): This page is the explicit trust-boundary analysis for disrobe.

## Integrations

- [GitHub Action](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/github-action.html): disrobe ships a composite GitHub Action that downloads the matching release binary, runs the selected command against one path, validates the emitted SARIF, and uploads that report to GitHub code scanning.
- [pre-commit hook](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/pre-commit.html): The pre-commit hook scans staged files and rejects a commit when a configured detector identifies a packed or protected artifact.
- [MCP server](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/mcp.html): disrobe ships a Model Context Protocol server so MCP clients can drive deobfuscation and decompilation directly as tools.
- [Editor plugins](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/editor-plugins.html): The editors/ directory contains plugins for VS Code, IDA Pro, Ghidra, and Binary Ninja.

## Project

- [Contributing](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/contributing.html): This guide covers building, testing, and extending Disrobe, including the evidence required for recovery claims.
- [Security](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/security.html): Report a vulnerability privately through GitHub's advisory channel, never in a public issue: <https://github.com/1-3-7/disrobe/security/advisories/new>.
- [Legal](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/legal.html): This page states the project's legal policy, its per-protector stances, and the takedown channel.

## Optional

- [The disrobe playground](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/playground/): decompile a .pyc, scan a pickle, and summarize a .wasm entirely client-side in the browser.
